title: Counting IV hours at mL/hour on a chart
blurb: Count hourly IV entries on a fluid chart correctly, including rate changes and midnight, and turn them into mL.
question: A fluid chart records IV fluid at 125 mL/hour at every hour from 0600 to 1100. What is the total IV input?

teach.h: Every hourly entry adds the rate
teach.body: Formal rule: IV input = rate (mL/hour) × number of hourly entries at that rate. On a chart, entries from one time to another, both included, number (later hour − earlier hour) + 1. Plain English: the IV column shows the rate in every hour it ran, so each entry is worth that many mL. Count the entries, multiply, then add each rate block.
teach.cite: FACTS.md section 4 (hourly IV input); Pearson practice charts

teach.caption: Four entries, not three: 12 − 9 + 1 = 4, so 400 mL.

steps.label: Split into rate blocks
steps.sub: A new block at each rate change

teach.h: Worked example: Chloe on the children's ward
teach.body: Chloe, 6, has IV fluids at 58 mL/hour entered 0100 to 0800, then 30 mL/hour entered 0900 to 1600. Block 1: 8 − 1 + 1 = 8 entries × 58 = 464 mL. Block 2: 16 − 9 + 1 = 8 entries × 30 = 240 mL. Total IV = 704 mL. Sense-check: 16 hours averaging about 44 mL/hour is roughly 700 mL.

teach.caption: Across midnight, list the hours: 2400 is followed by 0100.

teach.text: The fencepost error: subtracting the clock times gives the gaps between entries, not the number of entries. 0600 to 0900 is 3 hours of gaps but 4 entries. Add 1, or list the hours and count them.

teach.body: Read how the stem describes the infusion. If it lists hourly chart entries, count the entries. If it says an infusion ran for a stated number of hours (for example "5 hours" or "from 0800 until stopped at 1300"), multiply the rate by that duration instead. A bag recorded only on completion is one entry of the whole bag volume.

items: Each hourly IV entry adds the rate in mL.
Entries from A to B inclusive = B − A + 1.
Across midnight, list the hours to count them.
Split rate changes into blocks and add them.
Classic error: counting one hour too few (fencepost).

summary: You can now count inclusive hourly IV entries, handle rate changes and midnight, and convert them into total IV input in mL. You can also avoid the fencepost error that drops one hour.

B.q: A person's chart records intravenous 0.9% sodium chloride at 100 mL/hour, entered at 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600, 0700, 0800; then 0.9% sodium chloride at 50 mL/hour, entered at 0900, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1400. What is the total intravenous input?

whyNot.1: Used 100 mL/hour for all 14 entries; the rate fell at 0900.
whyNot.2: Counted 5 entries at 50 mL/hour instead of 6.

B.q: A baby's 24-hour chart records intravenous 10% glucose at 20 mL/hour, entered at 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600, 0700, 0800, 0900, 1000, and milk feeds: 0700 120 mL, 1100 150 mL, 1500 150 mL, 1900 150 mL, 2300 120 mL. What is the total input?
B.why: IV = 10 × 20 = 200 mL. Feeds = 690 mL. Total input = 890 mL.

whyNot.2: Counted the IV for all 24 hours.

C.q: Mr Hughes's 24-hour chart shows: Intravenous: one unit of red cells, 280 mL, recorded as 140 mL at 1000 and 140 mL at 1100; then 0.9% sodium chloride at 75 mL/hour, entered at 1300, 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, 1800, 1900, 2000. Oral: 0800 200 mL, 1400 150 mL, 1800 200 mL. Urine: 0600 350 mL, 1200 300 mL, 1800 400 mL, 2400 300 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.
C.why: IV = 280 + 8 × 75 = 880 mL. Oral = 550 mL. Input = 1430 mL. Output = 1350 mL. Balance = +80 mL.

whyNot.1: Counted 7 entries at 75 mL/hour instead of 8.
whyNot.3: Counted the 280 mL unit of red cells twice.

C.q: A child's 24-hour chart records intravenous 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose at 52 mL/hour, entered at 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600; then the same fluid at 26 mL/hour, entered at 0700, 0800, 0900, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, 1800, 1900, 2000, 2100, 2200, 2300, 2400. Oral: 1000 60 mL, 1400 80 mL, 1800 100 mL. Wet nappies weighed (1 g = 1 mL): 0400 110 g, 0900 95 g, 1300 120 g, 1700 105 g, 2200 130 g. Vomit: 0800 40 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.
C.why: IV = 6 × 52 + 18 × 26 = 780 mL. Oral = 240 mL. Input = 1020 mL. Output = 560 + 40 = 600 mL. Balance = +420 mL.

whyNot.2: Counted 17 entries at 26 mL/hour; 0700 to 2400 is 18.
whyNot.3: Counted 5 entries at 52 mL/hour; 0100 to 0600 is 6.

What is the total intravenous input?

whyNot.1: Counted 11 entries at 80 mL/hour instead of 12.

reteach.title: List the hours and count them
reteach.question: IV at 100 mL/hour entered from 0800 to 1300 inclusive: how much?

blocks.text: 13 − 8 = 5 counts the gaps between the hours, not the entries; it gives 500 mL, which is 100 mL short.

explain.body: Entries from A to B, both included = B − A + 1.
